state: The language repository defines .can records and operations plus attached # descriptions. The human has asked for automatic internal reference material for developers and integrators, while challenging the value of translated descriptions. Inspection finds that scenario descriptions feed editor hover as base prose and that the MCP operation table drops their locale variants even though scenario metadata retains them. Fields use a separate literal-only @{desc} input annotation. Page descriptions do render through locale-aware browser metadata. Existing machinery handles quoted text with keyed translations, message lowering, and language fallback; an actual documentation CLI is absent. A suggested compact field form is desc="Base"@{nl="Dutch"}; its parser slot and translated MCP field path would be new work. The first reference audience is explicitly internal developers/integrators. It must reflect declarations faithfully, avoid source duplication, preserve value and permission behavior, and distinguish source intent from implemented capability. Documentation must not manufacture effects, claim examples executed, or turn prose into access rules. There is currently no verified demand for reading the reference in multiple languages. Options that remove description localization still retain translations used by UI captions, messages and page presentation. These facts describe present code and proposed work, not benchmarked runtime behavior.

description_policy.instructions: Select the most defensible description-localization policy for this internal reference request, weighing real user benefit, author effort, engineering cost and source fidelity evenly across the alternatives.

criteria.source_only: Build a source-derived internal reference with deterministic rendering and descriptions in their original language. Drop localized declaration-description variants but keep translations for real UI captions, messages and page metadata. This minimizes translation obligations and representation work, at the expense of reference descriptions for non-source-language readers.
criteria.optional_shared: Build that deterministic reference using one static description contract shared by # and inline desc=. Preserve optional language variants, render an explicitly requested documentation locale through existing fallback, and permit the same descriptions to be resolved for MCP. No translation quota follows from supporting variants. Extra compiler/interface plumbing and locale checks are required; translations are useful when actual readers need them.
criteria.ai_first: Use an AI writer to author internal reference prose from located declaration facts, with citations and human-reviewed translation drafts. Keep real UI localization and the same restrictions on runtime authority and testing claims. It can connect workflows more fluently, but entails nondeterministic output, inference review and model operating cost.
